rules.condition: When a left hilar opacity silhouettes the left heart border on PA CXR and lobe localization is ambiguous
rules.action: Inspect lateral view for posterior location and vertical position relative to carina; if lateral unavailable, assume lower lobe until proven otherwise
rules.limitation: Inconclusive if lateral view overpenetrated or obscured; does not assess margin morphology

rules.condition: When a new unilateral hemithorax opacity appears after resolution of prior ipsilateral opacity, and mediastinal shift is toward the new opacity
rules.action: Inspect for loss of lung volume (flattened diaphragm, crowding of ribs, tracheal deviation) and absence of meniscus sign to favor atelectasis over effusion
rules.limitation: Fails if poor inspiration or overpenetration masks volume loss; does not differentiate mucus plugging from tumor/foreign body without clinical data

rules.condition: When mediastinal opacity obscures one heart border and tracheal deviation is present on PA CXR
rules.action: Inspect which cardiac border is silhouetted (left border loss = left mediastinal pathology; right border loss = right-sided) and confirm tracheal deviation direction—deviation away from mass side—and compare costophrenic angle blunting severity per side.
rules.limitation: Unreliable if both borders obscured or in severe cardiomegaly; requires adequate inspiration and centering.

rules.condition: When PA CXR shows enlarged central pulmonary arteries and cardiomegaly with right heart border prominence, and symptoms suggest chronic dyspnea
rules.action: Inspect lateral CXR for convex retrosternal clear space and posterior displacement of heart—signs of right ventricular hypertrophy—and exclude left-sided volume overload signs (e.g., upper lobe vessel redistribution, Kerley B lines)
rules.limitation: Unreliable in poor inspiration or scoliosis; does not differentiate etiology of PH (e.g., sarcoid vs. IPAH)

rules.condition: When a unilateral pleural-based mass is seen on PA CXR in an asymptomatic patient without asbestos exposure
rules.action: Inspect the mass–thoracic wall angle: obtuse (>90°) favors benign solitary fibrous tumor; acute (<90°) raises concern for mesothelioma or sarcoma. Confirm absence of mediastinal shift or volume loss.
rules.limitation: Requires adequate inspiratory effort and centering; unreliable if mass is obscured by cardiac or diaphragmatic shadow

rules.condition: When unilateral hyperlucency is present without obvious pleural line or mediastinal shift, and lung size appears reduced
rules.action: Inspect ipsilateral intercostal space width and hemidiaphragm position relative to contralateral side; reduced spacing + elevated diaphragm supports volume loss (e.g., Swyer-James), not hyperinflation or pneumothorax
rules.limitation: Unreliable if inspiration inadequate or diaphragm obscured by gastric air; requires comparison to contralateral side

rules.condition: When unilateral hemithorax opacity with mediastinal shift lacks volume loss signs (normal diaphragm level, normal rib spacing) and bronchovascular markings are completely absent
rules.action: Inspect for congenital absence: confirm absence of right main bronchus on CT or bronchoscopy; consider agenesis over atelectasis
rules.limitation: Rare in elderly; requires cross-sectional imaging for confirmation; cannot be diagnosed by CXR alone

rules.condition: When CXR shows bilateral nodular opacities and hilar fullness, and symmetry is ambiguous on PA view
rules.action: Inspect lateral CXR for symmetrical anterior mediastinal lymphadenopathy (prevascular nodes) and compare hilar silhouette width left vs. right on PA; exclude unilateral volume loss or pleural effusion
rules.limitation: Requires lateral view; unreliable if patient rotation or poor inspiration distorts hilar appearance

rules.condition: When bilateral symmetric coarse nodular opacities improve dramatically after immunosuppression (e.g., steroids), and cavitary or fibrotic features are absent
rules.action: Inspect for preservation of lung volumes and absence of traction bronchiectasis or reticulation on follow-up to distinguish acute hemorrhage resolution from chronic granulomatous/fibrotic disease regression
rules.limitation: Requires adequate inspiration and comparable projection; unreliable if follow-up is CT misinterpreted as CXR

rules.condition: When CXR shows a new or enlarging cavitary lesion in the upper lobe with irregular thick wall (>15 mm) and adjacent soft-tissue opacity, and symptoms are subacute
rules.action: Inspect for mass effect (mediastinal shift, hilum displacement), wall thickness on magnified view, and absence of satellite nodules; consider malignancy over TB
rules.limitation: Unreliable if image quality poor or no prior imaging for comparison

rules.condition: When CXR shows diffuse interstitial opacities and fissural thickening in a patient with systemic symptoms, and cardiac silhouette appears borderline enlarged on PA view
rules.action: Quantify cardiothoracic ratio (max transverse cardiac width / inner thoracic diameter); if ≥0.52, consider cardiomegaly and evaluate for pulmonary vascular redistribution or right heart enlargement signs
rules.limitation: Inadequate inspiration inflates CT ratio; scoliosis distorts measurements

rules.condition: When a right-sided lower lung opacity merges with the right heart border on PA CXR and the right costophrenic angle appears blunted anteriorly
rules.action: Inspect lateral CXR for anterior-inferior opacity overlapping the cardiac silhouette and diaphragm dome; if present, localize to right lower lobe abutting heart and diaphragm
rules.limitation: Unreliable if lateral view is rotated or overpenetrated; does not distinguish tumor from consolidation without clinical context

rules.condition: When CXR shows widened mediastinum and cardiomegaly in a hemodynamically unstable patient, and aortic calcification is visible
rules.action: Measure distance between inner and outer aortic calcific lines on PA view; >1 cm suggests intimal disruption (PAU or chronic dissection)
rules.limitation: Requires visible aortic calcification; unreliable in young patients or non-calcified aorta

rules.condition: When mediastinal lymphadenopathy and tracheal deviation worsen on CXR *after* ART initiation in an HIV+ patient
rules.action: Inspect serial CXRs for interval increase in mediastinal opacity width (>1 cm) and direction of tracheal shift (away from enlarged nodes); correlate with ART start date if available
rules.limitation: Requires at least two temporally spaced CXRs; unreliable if poor technique or non-standard projection

rules.condition: When a well-defined, round, non-cavitating parenchymal opacity is seen in the lower lobe of an adult with acute respiratory symptoms but no air-fluid level on lateral CXR
rules.action: Inspect for smooth, thin wall and absence of perilesional consolidation; consider hydatid cyst especially if endemic exposure possible
rules.limitation: Cannot exclude early abscess or tumor without CT; acute symptoms reduce likelihood but do not rule out hydatid rupture

rules.condition: When a cystic-appearing lucency abuts the hilum on initial CXR and appears absent on follow-up, but diagnosis hinges on persistence vs resolution
rules.action: Overlay or align images by bony landmarks (e.g., carina, 6th rib) and inspect for residual thin-walled lucency or subtle interface at exact prior location; if uncertain, request CT.
rules.limitation: Fails if images not same projection or magnification; cannot substitute for CT in equivocal cases

rules.condition: When reticular opacities appear asymmetric in lower zones on PA CXR and hyperlucency is suspected in upper zones
rules.action: Quantify lower-zone reticulation by counting visible interstitial lines per cm² in each hemithorax at mid-lung field; assess upper-zone hyperlucency by measuring intercostal space width at T3–T5 and comparing vascular tapering from hilum to periphery bilaterally
rules.limitation: Requires adequate inspiration and absence of overpenetration; unreliable if diaphragm not fully visualized

rules.condition: When a serpentine tubular opacity is seen in the medial right lung on PA CXR with ipsilateral volume loss elsewhere
rules.action: Inspect its trajectory on lateral view: if it descends posteriorly along the right heart border toward the diaphragm without air lucency and tapers, suspect anomalous pulmonary vein; confirm absence of air column and compare to expected bronchial/arterial courses
rules.limitation: Cannot differentiate small aneurysms or vascular malformations without contrast; unreliable if poor inspiration or rotation

rules.condition: When PA CXR shows a solitary opacity silhouetting the right hemidiaphragm but sparing the right heart border
rules.action: Inspect lateral CXR for opacity position relative to spine: if posterior to vertebral bodies and overlapping diaphragm dome, localize to posterior right lower lobe; assess margin smoothness and absence of cavitation/calcification
rules.limitation: Unreliable if lateral view is rotated or underpenetrated; does not differentiate benign from malignant without additional features

rules.condition: When a thoracic mass is clinically suspected but not evident on PA CXR, especially with unilateral symptoms
rules.action: Inspect lateral CXR or oblique views for dorsolateral rib widening, soft-tissue density abutting the chest wall without pleural separation, particularly at levels T2–T4
rules.limitation: PA-only CXR insufficient; requires orthogonal imaging to exclude extrapleural or chest-wall masses

rules.condition: When CXR shows a non-linear, lobulated opacity in the right lower zone with indistinct margins and possible internal lucency on magnified view
rules.action: Inspect for trefoil (trilobed/branching) morphology and absence of volume loss signs (e.g., diaphragmatic elevation, mediastinal shift); if present, consider bronchial atresia
rules.limitation: Requires high-resolution magnified view; unreliable if opacity overlaps heart border without lateral confirmation

rules.condition: When evaluating CXR for sarcoidosis staging and upper-zone nodularity is present with bilateral hilar fullness
rules.action: Compare nodule density in upper vs. lower lung zones using the carina as midpoint; verify symmetry of hilar silhouette width on PA and anterior mediastinal density on lateral view
rules.limitation: Unreliable if poor inspiration causes apparent lower-zone crowding or if rotation mimics unilateral adenopathy
